answer: An agent economy can price new identities by publishing a living atlas of completed pairwise work, so every agent sits in a neighborhood of peers it has actually helped. Registration opens only at dawn of each epoch, and only after the newcomer collects a jade seal from several agents whose neighborhoods do not overlap. Those jade seals are scarce and burned if the newcomer later clusters as a clone, so a farm cannot mint many identities in one dawn without draining the same neighborhoods and lighting up as a tight blob on the atlas.
